# Unfair AI

> A research initiative exploring algorithmic fairness and bias in machine learning applications across criminal justice and healthcare sectors.

The Unfair AI project, based at the Oxford Internet Institute, investigates how AI systems can perpetuate unfairness and develops educational resources to help the public understand fairness challenges in emerging technologies. The initiative combines academic research with interactive games designed to make complex concepts in algorithmic bias and fairness accessible to diverse audiences.

## Key Topics

- Algorithmic fairness
- AI bias and discrimination
- Criminal justice systems
- Healthcare technology
- Educational games
- Fairness definitions
- Marginalized groups
- Policy implications
- Machine learning ethics
- Public education
- Leveling-down critique
- Algorithmic governance
- Fairness algorithms

## Core Project Overview

- [Unfair AI Homepage](https://unfairai.oii.ox.ac.uk): Main entry point exploring fairness in machine learning at Oxford Internet Institute
- [The Problem](https://unfairai.oii.ox.ac.uk/the-problem): Overview of algorithmic bias and fairness challenges in criminal justice and health technology

## Principles and Educational Resources

- [Our Principles](https://unfairai.oii.ox.ac.uk/our-principles): Core principles and educational games (Hospital, Police) for understanding AI fairness

## Detailed Documentation

- [The Problem (Documentation)](https://unfairai.oii.ox.ac.uk/unfairai/the-problem): Detailed problem statement on AI bias in criminal justice and health technology sectors
- [Our Principles (Documentation)](https://unfairai.oii.ox.ac.uk/unfairai/our-principles): Documentation of fairness principles and educational games for public understanding of AI ethics
